records.summary: I. Organisation Background Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe was founded in 1952, and is represented by 9 national and round 300 regional and local associations throughout the Federal Republic of Germany. Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe is a chapter of the Johanniter Order and a registered association in accordance with German legislature. Besides domestic obligations (like Emergency Medical Services, Civil Protection, and social services) the statutory duties and responsibilities of Johanniter also include international humanitarian assistance. In its international humanitarian work, Johanniter is committed to act responsible and fair. Together with donors, colleagues and project partners, we approach different cultures and populations with respect, integrity and commitment. Our highest priority is to act according to the needs of the most vulnerable people. We mainly focus on three areas of work: primary health care, disaster response and preparedness, and rehabilitation of people with disability. Sustainability is of particular importance to us: We aim to improve the living conditions of people in distress in the short, mid and long term. records.title: Consultancy: Mid-Term Review of the BELIEVE Project.
records.summary: Background CBM Global Disability Inclusion is seeking a consultancy firm to undertake the mid-term review of the Bungoma Enhancing Localised, Inclusive, Efficient, Vision Engagement (BELIEVE) Project. BELIEVE is a KES 79 million inclusive eye health project implemented in Bungoma County by InterChristian Fellowships’ Evangelical Mission (IcFEM Mission), through Dreamland Mission Hospital, in partnership with the County Government of Bungoma, Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) and other health, rehabilitation and referral partners, supported By CBM Global Disability Inclusion. The project runs from March 2025 to December 2027. Its interventions cover improving accessibility of eye health services, community eye screening and treatment, referral and follow-up, rehabilitation, provision of assistive devices and psychosocial support, economic empowerment for specified groups, community-led advocacy, health-system strengthening and organisational capacity development. BACKGROUND The Refugee Consortium of Kenya (RCK) is a public benefit organization established to respond to the protection, rights and justice needs of refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, other forcibly displaced populations and host communities in Kenya. Over the years, RCK has evolved from a primarily service-oriented organization into an increasingly influential national actor working across protection, justice, governance, peace and social justice, women and girls’ empowerment, mental health and psychosocial support, institutional development, advocacy and systems strengthening. RCK’s current Strategic Plan 2023–2027 was developed around the vision of “A just and inclusive society for all the displaced and host populations”, with a mission to protect and promote the well-being, voice and dignity of displaced and host populations. Its strategic goal is to promote a safe environment in which displaced and host populations access justice and protection and are empowered to achieve their full potential. records.title: Fieldwork Consultancy for the SGBV Care Pathway Study (Addis Ababa)
records.summary: Tiko Africa Ethiopia invites qualified consultants or firms to carry out a mixed-methods study on screening, service readiness, quality of care and access barriers along the SGBV care pathway for adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) aged 15–24 in Addis Ababa. The consultant will lead the study from data collection through analysis and reporting. 1. Background Tiko is an African non-profit organisation addressing the “Triple Threat” facing adolescent girls and young women in Sub-Saharan Africa: early pregnancy, HIV and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). The Triple Threat package, delivered through Tiko’s technology-enabled, community-driven platform, is Tiko’s standard programme in all of its intervention areas. In Addis Ababa, Tiko supports screening, care and referral for survivors of SGBV, and for young women identified through transactional or survival sex screening under the Dignified Livelihoods Initiative (DILI), which adds livelihood support to the Triple Threat package. records.title: PF No. and Title: PR 989 – Call for proposals for the Implementation of an Endline Evaluation on the changes in coverage and incremental costs of GIS.
records.summary: Helen Keller International (Helen Keller Intl) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to saving and improving the sight and lives of the world's vulnerable by combating the causes and consequences of blindness, poor health and malnutrition. Helen Keller Intl invites all eligible Bidders to submit their technical and financial proposals to support Helen Keller in implementing an endline evaluation scheduled for February 2027 to measure the changes in vitamin A supplementation (VAS), deworming, and maternal and child health (MCH) service coverage since the November 2024 baseline, and to assess the incremental costs and potential value for money of integrating GIS-informed targeting and work planning into existing routine service delivery in Narok North and Central Sub-Counties, Narok County. The purpose of this Request for Proposals (RFP) is to select a vendor that will provide best value to Helen Keller Intl, when both technical and cost factors are combined.
